title: Synaptic clustering emerges from learning and supports covariance discrimination (Dendrinet)
why: Most on-topic paper. E and I functional synapse clusters emerge on dendrites through learning, essentially the RO1.2 E:I question. Biggest scoop risk: pin down exactly what they don't do.

title: Dynamics of specialization in neural modules under resource constraints
why: Structural modules only specialise when inputs are separable and resources are tight. Multisensory tasks with a limited bank of neuron shapes meet both conditions; their probing and ablation measures (normalised to chance) could be used on evolved networks. Gradient-trained RNN modules, parity task on MNIST digit pairs.

title: Dendrites endow artificial neural networks with accurate, robust and parameter-efficient learning
why: Closest precedent and the baseline to beat. Dendritic structure is a fixed mask; Marcus wants morphology to be learned. That difference is the novelty claim.

title: Partial recurrence enables robust and efficient computation
why: pRNNs: all 128 combinations of 7 optional pathways, trained with deep Q-learning on multisensory mazes. Only memoryless networks fail the track maze with a gap, which is the same result as the motif EA. Basis of my pRNN perturbation project.

title: Evolving Modular Neural Networks (UROP report)
why: The A1 method itself. Swapping the bank of 3-node motifs for a bank of neuron morphologies is the first move.
notes: Replicated in my repo (lakshaa-s/morphological_nets): matched EA vs NEAT rerun, distribution analysis, reference levels, sweep, HyperNEAT. See REPLICATION.md.

title: Nonlinear fusion is optimal for a wide class of multisensory tasks
why: Marcus's multisensory tasks; the natural first tasks for the synthetic-neuron bank.

title: Spatially embedded recurrent neural networks reveal widespread links between structural and functional neuroscience findings
why: Astle lab: networks embedded in space learn sparse, local wiring through a wiring-cost penalty (learned locality, vs LM-RNNs' fixed mask). Read before the Astle visit.

title: Single cortical neurons as deep artificial neural networks
why: Core reference in Marcus's research statement: how much computation a single morphologically detailed neuron performs.

title: How neuronal morphology impacts the synchronisation state of neuronal networks
why: Strongest disease link: arbour size alone flips network synchrony, tied to epilepsy susceptibility. Models are biophysical, not task-trained: does it hold in trained morphological networks? Pairs with the pRNN seizure-like perturbation work.

title: Connectome-constrained networks predict neural activity across the fly visual system
why: Method for constraining networks with connectome data, then training them on a task. Read the full paper, not the research briefing.

title: Winning the lottery with neural connectivity constraints: faster learning across cognitive tasks with spatially constrained sparse RNNs
why: Introduces Mod-Cog (up to 132 tasks from Yang et al. 2019, two input rings = two modalities) and locality-masked RNNs (LM-RNNs). Candidate stage-two task suite; needs Marcus's agreement.

title: Neural heterogeneity promotes robust learning
why: Methods template: trainable per-neuron parameters, heterogeneity measured as robustness. Morphology is a richer kind of heterogeneity. Goodman lab.

title: Task representations in neural networks trained to perform many cognitive tasks
why: The 20 cognitive tasks Mod-Cog extends; networks form task-specialised clusters, a specialisation result to compare with evolved morphology.

title: Evolving neural networks through augmenting topologies (NEAT)
why: The NEAT baseline in Charlotte's comparison: historical markings, speciation, starting minimal.

title: Retinal Connectomics: A Review
why: How retinal circuits remodel in degeneration. Pathoconnectome datasets are a concrete candidate for building from disease-model sets.

title: Illuminating search spaces by mapping elites (MAP-Elites)
why: Quality-diversity method suggested at Dan's lab meeting; my archive-immigrant test showed no effect (41/50 vs 42/50). Marcus: not a necessity.

title: Context-dependent computation by recurrent dynamics in prefrontal cortex
why: Classic gradient-trained RNN model of a psychophysics task (context-dependent integration).

title: A hypercube-based encoding for evolving large-scale neural networks (HyperNEAT)
why: CPPNs set weights from neuron positions; my matched HyperNEAT baseline beats NEAT and chance but solves no image runs (results in repo).
